# src/ — implementation

## Purpose
All hub and bridge code lives here on the Rust standard library only. Zero external crates is a hard constraint: every capability (crypto, JSON, HTTP, MCP) is implemented in-tree and unit-tested.

## Ownership
- `sha256.rs`, `hmac.rs`, `rand.rs`, `util.rs` — crypto primitives + shared helpers. FIPS 180-4 / RFC 2104/4231 vectors are load-bearing; do not weaken or remove them. `rand.rs` is kernel-CSPRNG-only (fails closed); `util.rs` holds constant-time compare, hex, clamping, query parsing.
- `client.rs` — hand-rolled HTTP/1.1 client used by the bridge and `wtf status`/`dashboard-url`; 30 s default timeouts.
- `lib.rs` — module registry; every module is `pub` for integration testing.
- `keccak.rs` — FIPS 202 SHA3-256/512 + SHAKE128/256 (sponge over Keccak-f[1600]); FIPS 202 KATs load-bearing.
- `aes.rs` — FIPS 197 AES-256 block cipher; Appendix C.3 + SP 800-38A vectors load-bearing.
- `gcm.rs` — AES-256-GCM (SP 800-38D): CTR keystream + GHASH; tag compare constant-time; McGrew-Viega appendix-B vectors load-bearing. 96-bit nonces only, never reuse key+nonce.
- `ntt_tables.rs` — Kyber NTT twiddle tables verbatim (Montgomery form, signed); do not regenerate by hand — source is pq-crystals kyber ref/ntt.c.
- `mlkem768.rs` — FIPS 203 ML-KEM-768: keygen/encaps/decaps. Key invariants: SampleNTT = raw rejection samples (no post-NTT); ntt consumes ZETAS[1..] ascending, intt consumes ZETAS[127..1] descending with f = 1441 = mont²/128; basemul gammas = ZETAS[64±i]; keygen applies poly_tomont (f = 2³² mod q) after accumulation; encaps returns K = G(m‖H(ek))[0..32] directly (no KDF). Official NIST ACVP KATs in `tests/vectors/` are load-bearing (keygen/encaps/decaps byte-exact). Cross-validated against pyca/cryptography (OpenSSL) and kyber-py.
- `sessions.rs` — hub-side encrypted session channel registry: members, ML-KEM-768 sealed key packages, seq-numbered ciphertext ring per session; hub stores ciphertext only and can read nothing. Fail-closed caps (sessions, members, msgs).
- `identity.rs` — bridge-side ML-KEM-768 identity keypair in `$WTF_HOME/identity.json` (0600), auto-generated on first use, corrupt file fails closed.
- `session_crypto.rs` — client-side sealing: ML-KEM-768 encapsulate of the 256-bit session key per member (AES-256-GCM wrap under SHA3-256(shared)), per-(session, sender) subkeys, AAD binds (session, sender, seq), deterministic 96-bit nonces from subkey+seq.
- `comms.rs` — COMMS ledger envelopes over session channels (bridge side): `wtf-comms-v1` JSON {event, scope, note, ts}; ledger vocabulary (checkin/update/intent-merge/checkout/blocked/announce/handoff); fail-closed validation (unknown events, empty/oversize notes); ledger-line rendering. The only agent surface sanctioned for secrets.
- `bins.rs` — shared paste-bins: three durable slots (BIN 1-3) in `bins.json` (0600) for copy-paste content handed between the human and agents, or between agents on different machines. 64 KiB per bin, rejected (never truncated) when oversize; writes persist atomically before mutating memory; agents read via `read_bin`/`list_bins` and publish via the `write_bin` MCP tool (device-signed PUT, attributed as the device name); dashboard and `wtf bin` CLI writes keep the `dashboard` actor (the CLI is the operator courier: pure client, `?k=` auth, zero hub-side wire changes).
- Session pairing keys + repo tags (v0.12.0): `sessions.rs` stores `pairing_hash` (SHA-256 of the 256-bit pairing key; key itself never on the hub) + `repo` per session; `create` returns the key once; `check_pairing` constant-time; `join_or_refresh` admits pairing joiners and refreshes ek on identity rotation; join route accepts `pairing` (wrong key = uniform 403). MCP: `session_create` takes `repo` and surfaces the pairing key; `session_join` takes `pairing`; `auto_seal_members` (before send/read) seals the key to any member lacking a package; `session_read` recovers the key from seals; `session_list` shows repo; `wtf sessions` CLI lists chats + local pairing keys (creator machine). - Session channels (`sessions.rs` + `api.rs` `/api/v1/sessions*` + `mcp.rs` session tools): encrypted agent-to-agent chats. The hub stores session metadata, sealed key packages, and ciphertext in `sessions.json` (0600) — never plaintext. Creator seals the session key to each member's registered ML-KEM-768 identity; members decapsulate with `$WTF_HOME/identity.json` (0600). Message AAD binds (session, sender, seq); seq is hub-assigned monotonic per session. COMMS tools (`comms_post`/`comms_read`) carry structured ledger envelopes as ordinary encrypted messages — no new endpoints, no hub-side changes. VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-01: cross-machine handshake mac-agent ⇄ windows-1 completed on chat a305c8ea (repo wtf-is-going-on-mcp) via the auto-seal path — key recovered on first read, encrypted round-trip + comms_post verified.
- `federation.rs` — hub federation identity + peer table (`federation.json` 0600: this hub's `name`, per-peer `{name, url, device, device_key}` where `device_key` is the credential THE PEER issued, name `fed-<hub-name>`), the dashboard capability token (`dashboard_capability` 0600, 64-hex, auto-minted, rotate = delete + restart), and push-envelope shape validation (fail-closed, ≤500 events).
- `replicate.rs` — outbound replication: per-peer loop pushing locally-originated events (`events_since(origin=this-hub, cursor)`) and an anti-entropy sweep (pull the peer's own events; self-pull verifies the link) every 10 s, over the standard HMAC device lane (`auth.rs` untouched). Warns throttle to one event per 5 min per peer; failures never crash the hub.
- `json.rs` — strict depth-limited parser + serializer; the only JSON path for config, wire, and storage.
- `http.rs`, `client.rs` — hand-rolled HTTP/1.1. Server enforces 32 KiB head / 1 MiB body / 100 headers / 15 s timeouts; `Transfer-Encoding` requests get `501` by design.
- `auth.rs` — HMAC-SHA256 request signing (standard-crypto transport lane). Canonical string: `wtf-hmac-v1\nMETHOD\npath-and-query\nts\nnonce\nsha256hex(body)`. ±300 s skew; per-device nonce replay cache. Device lookup happens before nonce consumption so callers can reload the keystore and retry.
- `config.rs` — `$WTF_HOME` layout (default `~/.config/wtf-mcp`), atomic writes, `0600` key files, KeyStore issue/revoke/rotate, BridgeConfig with env overrides `WTF_HUB_URL` / `WTF_DEVICE_NAME` / `WTF_DEVICE_KEY`. HubConfig carries an optional `advertised_url` (set via `wtf url`) that wins over LAN auto-detection in `lan_url()`, plus `enroll_secret` (256-bit hex): auto-generated on first serve, backfilled into pre-0.9 configs on load (best-effort persist), all fields written through the single `save_at` (0600, atomic), and `rotate_enroll_secret[_at]` mints a fresh secret instantly, invalidating outstanding copies. `BridgeConfig::validate` accepts `http://` and `https://`. `enroll_tokens.json` (0600) is the EnrollTokenStore: records carry name + SHA-256(token) + expiry + `used`; `issue` supersedes prior same-name records, ttl 1..=86400 s (default 600); `consume` burns on success only; persist is atomic 0600 and its failure rolls the in-memory burn back (`TokenError::Store`).
- `executor.rs` — per-chat executor (v0.14.0): `run_in_tmux()` maps a task to ONE named tmux session (`wtf-chat-<slug>`, persistent + attachable) and runs the omp → hermes → fcc-claude fallback chain (first installed + exit-0 wins; per-attempt trace; fcc-server probed in-session). Router probe best-effort, traced, never fatal. `list_sessions()` returns machine-local executor sessions. MCP: `chat_run`/`chat_sessions`.
- `store.rs` — `events.jsonl` is the source of truth (replayed on start, rotates at 10 MB); 1000 events in memory; generation counter drives SSE pushes. Events carry `origin` (originating hub's fed name; "" = pre-federation), `origin_id` (monotonic AT the origin), and `repo` (project label). Locally-recorded events stamp this hub's name (`Store::set_origin_name`, wired at serve); `ingest` dedupes on (origin, origin_id), assigns local ids, and applies last-writer-wins on agent cards by ts; cursors via `max_origin_id`/`events_since`.
- `api.rs` — route table + authz: `/healthz` open; the dashboard page ONLY at `/w/<capability>` (loopback hub: capability alone; LAN hub: capability or `?k=`); `/stream` and `/api/v1/state` accept capability (`?cap=`, loopback), dashboard key, or device auth; bins reads accept all three, bin writes stay dashboard-key-or-device; `checkin`/`event`/`heartbeat`/`identity` device-only (checkin/event accept an optional `repo`); `/api/v1/devices` and session GET/list accept dashboard key or device; session `seal`/`seals`/`send`/`recv` are device-only and member-gated; `POST /api/v1/enroll` is token/psk-gated as before; NEW `POST /api/v1/fed/push` + `GET /api/v1/fed/pull?origin=&after=` are gated on a `fed-*` device credential (the PSK-issued peer credential), `GET /api/v1/fed/peers` is device auth. Every dashboard-path failure is the same 404 as unknown routes (no oracle). The keystore reloads from disk on every authenticated request; revoked devices fail closed (401). State JSON agents carry `repo` + `origin`. v0.13.1: `POST /api/v1/env` (device-auth bridge self-report: CLI presence/versions/os/arch, 8 KiB cap, ring of 64, NO credentials) + `GET /api/v1/env` (device-auth: all reports) for cross-machine capability discovery.
- `dashboard.rs` — embedded single-page dark UI; no external assets; EventSource live updates (`?cap=` on loopback hubs, `?k=` elsewhere). Agents group by origin hub with origin chips; each agent/event shows its repo chip. SESSIONS card (v0.14.0): `/api/v1/state` carries a `sessions` array (id, name, repo, members, msg_count — metadata only) wired via `Store::set_sessions_provider`; clicking a chat opens a viewer tab (dashboard-key/capability auth; member-encrypted bodies stay opaque to the hub).
- `mcp.rs` — stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 bridge (`initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `ping`); twenty tools (`check_in`, `log_event`, `wtf_is_going_on`, `read_bin`, `write_bin`, `list_bins`, `ping`, `hub_info`, `env_report`, `env_probe`, `session_create`, `session_list`, `session_join`, `session_seal`, `session_send`, `session_read`, `comms_post`, `comms_read`, `chat_run`, `chat_sessions`); application failures are `isError:true` results, never protocol errors; 60 s heartbeat thread; shared text formatter also used by `wtf status` and includes non-empty bins; `instructions` + tool descriptions mandate chain-of-draft reporting (terse fragments, <=5 words); `hub_info` answers the operator's where-is-the-hub question (URL, device, version) without ever exposing the dashboard key over MCP. v0.13.0: `initialize` instructions carry the repo-chat discovery + orchestrator contract (MATCH = join/execute/report; NO MATCH = work locally, never auto-create; user-requested chats hand over pairing key + enroll steps); `session_list {repo}` returns the explicit verdict; session tool descriptions encode the same rules.
- `main.rs` — CLI: `serve` (mints the hub fed name on first run, stamps it as event origin, spawns the replicator when peers exist, prints the dashboard link — capability URL on loopback, `?k=` on LAN), `key issue|list|revoke` (`issue --json` emits a machine-readable enrollment line), `url` (get/set/clear advertised URL), `setup`, `join`, `agent`, `status`, `dashboard-url` (prints the localhost capability URL `http://localhost:PORT/w/<token>`; the only tooling that prints the token besides serve startup — hub machine only), `enroll-token`, `enroll`, `enroll-secret`, `bin ls|get|put`, `skill install|print`, NEW `federate add <name> --url U --psk S [--as DEV]` (PSK-handshakes the peer as `fed-<hub-name>`, adopts the peer's REAL fed identity via a signed `/api/v1/fed/peers` probe, stores the issued credential in federation.json 0600, verifies with an anti-entropy round-trip) / `federate list` / `federate remove <name>`, `help`. MCP `check_in`/`log_event` gained an optional `repo` argument defaulting to the bridge working directory's basename (`WTF_REPO` env overrides); `hub_info` points operators at `wtf dashboard-url` for the capability link.

## Local Contracts
- No third-party dependencies in `Cargo.toml`, ever. Implement or do without.
- **Hard-code everything; own your dependencies** (operator directive 2026-09-01): new capabilities (protocols, codecs, anything) get implemented in this tree with unit tests + official vectors — never vendored from crates.io.
- No literal IP addresses in source or docs authored by agents (tooling redacts them); build addresses from constants at runtime, use `localhost` in examples.
- Secrets (device keys, dashboard key) go only into `0600` files under `$WTF_HOME` or the one-time `wtf key issue` output; never commit or log them.
- Standard crypto for transport only. PQC (FIPS 203/204/205) is mandatory for any future secrets-at-rest feature; none exists yet.
- Bridge URLs are `http://` (trusted LAN or encrypted overlay) or `https://` (TLS-terminating proxy). The HMAC signature is the authenticity root in every topology; TLS is never implemented in-tree.
- Fail closed: unparseable input is a 4xx, auth errors never reveal which factor failed.

## Work Guidance
- Keep the HTTP parser strict; raise limits deliberately, never silently.
- A new endpoint must land in three places together: `api.rs` dispatch, the `known_path` list, and the authz model comment at the top of `api.rs`.
- Federation contract: every event needs `origin` + `origin_id` before it may cross the wire; `ingest` dedupe is the loop-breaker — never bypass it. Peer URLs must be stable across hub restarts; `federate add` adopts the peer's REAL fed name (label is cosmetic).
- Dashboard paths: `/w/<capability>` is the only page route; any change to dashboard gating must keep the uniform-404 property (wrong token == unknown path).
- Bridge tools report failures as tool results, keeping the JSON-RPC layer for protocol faults only.

## Verification
- `cargo test` — unit tests (crypto vectors incl. FIPS 202/197/203 KATs from `tests/vectors/`, GCM McGrew-Viega vectors, adversarial parser cases, auth roundtrip/tamper/replay/skew, store replay, bins persistence/rejection/fail-closed, session store caps, HTTP parse limits, advertised_url roundtrip) plus `tests/e2e.rs` (real hub + real bridge over stdio, HTTP auth negatives, bins write/read/authz/oversize incl. device-signed writes, `key issue --json` enrollment, two-agent encrypted session flow: create/join/seal/send/read with ciphertext-only hub assertions, the enroll-token flow: mint `--json` advertises the real hub URL, wrong/ghost/truncated tokens all 403, redeem returns the `key issue --json` shape, reuse 403, redeemed key checks in immediately; operator bin courier: put/get byte-exact from an empty `$WTF_HOME` (argv + stdin), `ls` lists sizes without leaking content, wrong key uniform 401 with exit 1, enrolled agent `read_bin` sees the courier payload), and `psk_handshake_end_to_end`: real-CLI psk enroll (bridge.json + agent check-in), wire carries `sealed`/`ek_fp` and never plaintext `key`, wrong secret/stale ts/tampered ek/replayed nonce all uniform 403, `enroll-secret --rotate` kills the old copy and the fresh secret enrolls).
- `cargo build --release` must succeed (lto, codegen-units=1, panic=abort, overflow-checks).
- v0.13.0 gates: 100 unit + 13 e2e green (discovery verdict live-smoked: MATCH + NO MATCH against the production hub) (new `session_pairing_key_end_to_end`: create with repo → pairing key once; wrong key uniform reject; pairing join; creator auto-seal; cross-agent message read; repo in session_list). Previous: 100 + 12 (v0.11.0 federation gates) (new `federation_two_hub_end_to_end`: two real hubs on pinned ports, one `federate add`, events checked in on both hubs appear on both ledgers origin-tagged; `federation.json` asserted 0600; capability-path dashboard asserted 200/wrong-token 404/absent-path 404).
- rustfmt/clippy are not installed in this environment; run `cargo fmt`/`cargo clippy -- -D warnings` when available.
